report.source_text: Renal biopsy findings revealed nine crescent formations and eight scleroses in 17 glomeruli. Endocapillary hypercellularity was also present. Inflammatory cells had infiltrated into the interstitium. Mild tubular atrophy with interstitial fibrosis was observed by light microscopy. In the mesangium, immunofluorescence assays revealed 2+ diffuse fine granular staining for IgA and 1+ staining for IgM and C3. Electron microscopy revealed dense deposits in the mesangial area (Figure 1A, B).

report.source_text: Two days after the renal biopsy was performed, serum creatinine levels increased from 3.9 mg/dL to 4.8 mg/dL. The patient was treated with prednisolone pulse therapy (250 mg twice daily) for 3 consecutive days; the dose was tapered to 1 mg/kg/day (Figure 2). Planned intravenous cyclophosphamide therapy was canceled because the patient developed abdominal symptoms on the fifth day of steroid treatment. He had watery diarrhea 10 times daily, and laboratory data revealed that he suffered from metabolic acidosis caused by severe diarrhea. Blood gas analysis showed the following parameters: pH 7.24, PaCO2 22.4, PaO2 82.6, and HCO3 9.7. His serum chloride level was 121 mmol/L; BUN and serum creatinine levels were 89 and 3.88 mg/dL, respectively. The patient was treated with 5-ASA (2 g/day) and loperamide (6 mg/day). In addition, intravenous fluid therapy was administered to restore volume loss. The watery diarrhea subsided in 2 weeks, and the patient was discharged.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male with a 2-year history of Crohn's disease (diagnosed June 2009, treated with 5-ASA and budesonide) presented to nephrology in March 2011 with dark loose stools, pale conjunctiva, facial puffiness, and lower extremity edema. Initial evaluation revealed hypertension (BP 137/96 mmHg), proteinuria (2+ on dipstick, worsened from 1+ in December 2010), microscopic hematuria, and acute renal dysfunction (BUN 30.3 mg/dL, creatinine 3.42 mg/dL). Kidney biopsy performed in March 2011 confirmed rapidly progressive IgAN with 9 crescents in 17 glomeruli, endocapillary hypercellularity, interstitial inflammation, and mild tubular atrophy with interstitial fibrosis on light microscopy. Immunofluorescence showed 2+ diffuse fine granular IgA deposits in the mesangium with 1+ IgM and C3 staining. Electron microscopy revealed electron-dense deposits in the mesangial area. Serologic workup excluded ANCA-associated vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, and other secondary causes of RPGN (negative ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, ASO, RF, cryoglobulin; normal complement levels C3/C4; mildly elevated serum IgA 492 mg/dL). Treatment with prednisolone pulse therapy (250 mg twice daily for 3 days) followed by taper to 1 mg/kg/day was initiated. Cyclophosphamide was canceled due to severe diarrhea exacerbation (10 times daily with metabolic acidosis). Patient was managed with 5-ASA (2 g/day) and loperamide (6 mg/day), with diarrhea subsiding in 2 weeks and discharge from hospital. By July 2011 (3 months post-treatment), renal function had improved (Cr 2.5 mg/dL, BUN 61.2 mg/dL) with persistent proteinuria (2+ dipstick, UPCR 1.8 mg/g). Maintenance immunosuppression was adjusted: azathioprine (100 mg/day) in September 2011, then switched to mycophenolate sodium (360 mg/day) in October 2011 due to bone marrow suppression. By December 2011, renal function was maintained (Cr 2.32 mg/dL, BUN 33.8 mg/dL) on mycophenolate sodium (360 mg/day) and deflazacort (12 mg/day) with stable intestinal symptoms.

Kidney biopsy performed in March 2011 confirmed rapidly progressive IgAN with 9 crescents in 17 glomeruli, endocapillary hypercellularity, interstitial inflammation, and mild tubular atrophy with interstitial fibrosis on light microscopy. Immunofluorescence showed 2+ diffuse fine granular IgA deposits in the mesangium with 1+ IgM and C3 staining. Electron microscopy revealed electron-dense deposits in the mesangial area. Serologic workup excluded ANCA-associated vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, and other secondary causes of RPGN (negative ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, ASO, RF, cryoglobulin; normal complement levels C3/C4; mildly elevated serum IgA 492 mg/dL). Treatment with prednisolone pulse therapy (250 mg twice daily for 3 days) followed by taper to 1 mg/kg/day was initiated. Cyclophosphamide was canceled due to severe diarrhea exacerbation (10 times daily with metabolic acidosis). Patient was managed with 5-ASA (2 g/day) and loperamide (6 mg/day), with diarrhea subsiding in 2 weeks and discharge from hospital. By July 2011 (3 months post-treatment), renal function had improved (Cr 2.5 mg/dL, BUN 61.2 mg/dL) with persistent proteinuria (2+ dipstick, UPCR 1.8 mg/g). Maintenance immunosuppression was adjusted: azathioprine (100 mg/day) in September 2011, then switched to mycophenolate sodium (360 mg/day) in October 2011 due to bone marrow suppression. By December 2011, renal function was maintained (Cr 2.32 mg/dL, BUN 33.8 mg/dL) on mycophenolate sodium (360 mg/day) and deflazacort (12 mg/day) with stable intestinal symptoms.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: 18-year-old male with Crohn's disease presenting with acute renal dysfunction, proteinuria, hematuria, and systemic edema
Kidney biopsy confirmed IgA-dominant glomerulonephritis with crescentic disease (9 crescents in 17 glomeruli), endocapillary hypercellularity, interstitial inflammation, and tubular atrophy
Immunofluorescence showed 2+ diffuse fine granular IgA deposits in mesangium with 1+ IgM and C3; electron microscopy revealed electron-dense mesangial deposits
Serologic workup excluded ANCA-associated vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, and other secondary causes (negative ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, ASO, RF, cryoglobulin; normal C3/C4; mildly elevated IgA 492 mg/dL)
Acute renal deterioration post-biopsy (Cr increased from 3.9 to 4.8 mg/dL within 2 days), consistent with rapidly progressive disease
Treatment with prednisolone pulse therapy (250 mg twice daily for 3 days) followed by taper; cyclophosphamide canceled due to severe diarrhea exacerbation
Renal function improved by July 2011 (Cr 2.5 mg/dL, BUN 61.2 mg/dL) and further stabilized by December 2011 (Cr 2.32 mg/dL, BUN 33.8 mg/dL) on mycophenolate sodium and deflazacort
